name: document-workspace
title: Document Workspace
description: A notes or docs workspace: an explorer, tabs, breadcrumb, toolbar, the document (edit or read), an aside for backlinks, properties and the outline, a status bar with the save state, an alert slot and Ctrl/Cmd+P quick open. Resizable, collapsible columns when its container is wide, drawers when narrow; named landmarks and toggles agents can press. Also DocumentOutline and DocumentQuickOpen.
docs: `<DocumentWorkspace document={mode === "edit" ? <MarkdownEditor ref={editor} …/> : <MarkdownView …/>} explorer tabs breadcrumb toolbar statusBar aside alert quickOpen={<DocumentQuickOpen items onOpen />} mode onModeChange editorRef={editor} headings={extractHeadings(markdown)} saveState storageKey>`. It fills its parent (`--document-workspace-height`, 100% by default) and decides its layout from its own width, never the viewport, so it works inside an app shell's `<main>` (in a `Shell`, give it `main="fill"` or the route `main: "fill"` and it fills the height left): at `narrow` (760 px) or less, the explorer and the aside are 20rem drawers that start closed; wider, they are resizable columns (`Resize files`, `Resize details` handles) that collapse from their toggles or the handle. `explorerOpen`/`onExplorerOpenChange` and `asideOpen`/`onAsideOpenChange` follow what is shown, and control it; turning narrow closes them and turning wide brings back the columns. A link in the explorer drawer closes it; pass `documentId` (the open document's slug or path) and the drawer also closes when it changes, whatever opened the document: a button in your tree, quick open, a wikilink or an agent. `useDocumentWorkspace().closeExplorer()` closes the drawer from your own tree (the wide column stays). `storageKey` remembers the columns' state and widths in localStorage (the drawers always start closed). Landmarks: the explorer is a `nav`, the aside an `aside`, the document a named region (`documentAs="main"` when the workspace is the page's main content); the toggles carry `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. The mode switch is a SegmentedControl; switching keeps the reading position by heading (from the editor's `getScrollLine` to the read view's headings and back). `saveState` (`saved`, `saving`, `unsaved`, `error`) is a polite `<output>` in the status bar; `alert` sits in an assertive region that is always there, so a conflict is read once when it appears (pass an `Alert` without `live`). `quickOpen` adds a Quick open button and `quickOpenShortcut` (`mod+p`, `false` to turn it off). `DocumentQuickOpen` searches in one of two ways. With `items`, it filters them in the browser by label and `keywords` (`filter`: `"fuzzy"` by default, `"contains"`, `"startsWith"` or a function); for a search of your own, pass `filter={false}`, `onQueryChange` and `status` (`"loading"`, `"error"`) and set `items` from its results, which are then listed as they are, so a note that matched on its body shows although its title lacks the query. With `source` (a `PageSource<T, { q?: string }>` from `@eskais/page-source`, as `ServerCombobox` takes) and `getItem`, it searches the server itself while it is open: the query goes out as `filter.q` once typing pauses (`debounce`, 200 ms), a newer query aborts the request in flight, the server's order is kept and the next page (`pageSize`, 20) loads at the end of the list. Loading and errors show in the list and are read out; `labels` takes `empty` (text or a function of the query), `loading`, `error` and `count`. `DocumentOutline` lists `headings`: in edit mode an entry puts the caret at the heading (`setSelection`, `scrollToLine`) and focuses the editor; in read mode it scrolls to the heading and focuses it, found by its `slug` (the `data-slug` `MarkdownView` renders), so a filtered `headings` list, like one without empty headings, still reveals the right one; `useDocumentWorkspace().revealHeading(heading)` does the same for your own outline. Drawers, quick open and menus give focus back to the document unless the action moved it: pass `useDocumentWorkspace().documentFocusTarget` as `finalFocus` to your own menus in `toolbar`. `editorRef` takes any `DocumentEditor` (`focus`, `scrollToLine`, `setSelection`, `getScrollLine`), which `MarkdownEditorHandle` is. All text is in `labels`.
